name: input
title: Input
description: A single-line text field whose invalid state is driven by aria-invalid.
docs:
## When to use - A single line of text the user types: email, name, slug, search, URL. - A field that needs a native input type (`email`, `password`, `tel`, `number`, `file`) and therefore native mobile keyboards. - Anywhere the browser's autofill, password manager, or form submission should work without a wrapper. ## When not to use - Multi-line text; use `textarea`. - A choice from a fixed list; use `select` (or `combobox` when the list is long). - A value the app controls entirely, like a generated id. Render text, not a disabled input. ## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/input ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input/input"; import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label/label"; export function WorkspaceName() { return (
); } ``` ## Examples ### Invalid `aria-invalid` is the only switch. The component renders the destructive border and ring; it never decides that the value is wrong. ```tsx

Enter a complete email address.

``` ### File input `file:` variants are already wired, so the native picker button picks up the tokens: ```tsx ``` ### Controlled, Base UI style ```tsx const [value, setValue] = useState(""); ; ``` ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------- | | `type` | `string` | – | Native input type. | | `value` | `string \| number \| readonly string[]` | – | Controlled value. | | `defaultValue` | same as `value` | – | Uncontrolled initial value. | | `onValueChange` | `(value: string, details) => void` | – | Base UI change callback, in addition to `onChange`. | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. | All native input props are forwarded, including `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, and `aria-*`. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). An input that grows, slides, or fades while the user types is a bug: it moves the caret under the user's eyes. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | `transition-[color,box-shadow]` exists for the focus ring and the invalid border. Both are colour/shadow state feedback on the design tokens, take no space, and do not run on mount. ## Validation and data ownership P11 draws the line: the component renders state, the user decides state. | The component does | You do | | ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | | Styles `aria-invalid="true"` and `data-invalid` | Deciding what "valid" means (required, format, length) | | Renders whatever `aria-describedby` points at | Writing the error text and the ids it lives on | | Forwards `required`, `readOnly`, `disabled`, `name` | Form state (react-hook-form, TanStack Form, server state) | | Keeps focus visible and keyboard-reachable | Submit, retry, error mapping, focus management | There is no `schema`, `resolver`, `validate`, or `rules` prop, and no validation library is imported. [Field](/components/field) shows how the invalid state and its message are wired. ## Accessibility - Base UI's input is field-aware: inside a `field`, it receives the label id and the description ids without extra wiring. - Always give it a name from a `label`; a placeholder is not a name. - `aria-invalid` plus a described error is the accessible failure state. Colour alone is never the signal. - Never set `outline: none` in `className`; the focus ring is the only affordance for keyboard users. ## Notes for AI - Use `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` — never an `error` prop or internal state. - Do not wrap the input in a div just to add a border; the component already owns the border, radius, and focus ring.
